take_homes: Start with one agent and split only for different access, dialect or stance. Three agents are not three times better.
Hand the synthesizer a framework (diagnosis, guiding policy, actions) so it picks instead of averaging. That worked better than rewording the prompt.
The seams between agents are where numbers get lost, and nothing in this module checks whether the final briefing is true.

monday.move: Run the wiki, docs and internet retrievers on the usage-pricing question, then have the synthesizer use the strategy kernel on the results, with the churn article flagged as untrusted.

monday.stop_condition: If one well-prompted agent gives the same quality, keep the single prompt. If the synthesis can't show where sources disagree, don't send it.
monday.blocker: The files sit in my local ~/Documents folder and the team has no shared place for them, so a teammate can't pick them up.

misconception.why: The framework changed the output more than any wording did, and the split tests (access, dialect, stance) are about structure rather than prompts. But the exercises were still mostly prompt pasting, so I'm only half convinced.

one_line: Good on when not to split an agent and on making the synthesizer commit to a view, but it says 'use one agent' three times and leaves me with a briefing I can't yet trust.
